# A Breakdown of Facebook Ad Types

Writing by [Massimo Chieruzzi](https://adespresso.com/guides/facebook-ads-beginner/facebook-ads-types/#)

# A Breakdown of Facebook Ad Types

In Chapter 3 of our Facebook Ads Guide, we’re going to discover all the different Facebook ad types.

You’ll find the answers to the following questions:

*   What basic ad formats are there on Facebook?
*   What Facebook ad types can I make from my Facebook Page?
*   What Facebook ad types can I make from my Ads Manager?
*   How can I use each Facebook ad type for my advertising goals?

By understanding your Facebook ad format and ad type options, you can design Facebook ads that cater to your specific audience and marketing goals — and make the most out of your Facebook advertising experience.

## Basic ad formats

A Facebook ad format is the basic layout of your ad: a single image with text, a video, a full-screen interactive experience, etc. There are only seven basic ad formats, but with these seven, you can design a huge number of ad types aimed at different advertising objectives.

In the section below, we will introduce the seven ad formats before expanding into the many ad types that you can make with them.

### **Image ads**

[Image ads](https://www.facebook.com/business/help/217010726413426?id=1240182842783684) are the most basic ad format. They contain only a single image and can be used in multiple different ad types, placements, and aspect ratios.

Image ads are easy to make and can effectively show off your product or service if you use high-quality photos. This ad format is a great all-around choice for almost any stage of your funnel, whether you want to grow your brand awareness or promote a sale to increase conversions.

Although image ads are a great all-around choice, they can also be limiting as you only have a single image to get your message across. When you want to demonstrate how your product works or show off multiple products, the single image format is not your best choice.

[Best practices](https://www.facebook.com/business/help/388369961318508?id=1240182842783684) for image ads:

*   Pay attention to aspect ratios, so your end product doesn’t get stretched or cut off.
*   Put in the effort to make quality images that stand out from the rest of Facebook.
*   Keep your message focused by using only as much text as you need.

Learn more about [image ad specs](https://www.facebook.com/business/help/755224297893936?id=1240182842783684).

[](https://adespresso.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/05/Facebook-advertising-01.png)

[_Source_](https://adespresso.com/blog/copy-testing-tools-strategies-increase-conversions/)

### **Video ads**

[Video ads](https://www.facebook.com/business/help/1381779698788633?id=603833089963720) use a single video to market a product or service.

Video advertising drives [high audience engagement](https://databox.com/videos-vs-images-in-facebook-ads), and even smaller companies can make simple videos to entertain and connect with their audience.

The only drawback to video ads is that they are time-consuming to make. If you have simple messages, then an image or carousel might do the job more efficiently.

[Best practices](https://www.facebook.com/business/help/144240239372256?id=603833089963720) for video ads:

*   Keep your videos short (Facebook suggests less than 15 seconds).
*   Start with a bang and get your audience engaged.
*   Read our full guide to effective [video ads on Facebook](https://adespresso.com/blog/facebook-video-ads-guide/).

Learn more about [video ad specs](https://www.facebook.com/business/help/1596868350601716?id=603833089963720).

[](https://adespresso.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/05/Facebook-advertising-02.png)

### **Slideshow ads**

[Slideshow ads](https://www.facebook.com/business/help/149759192130274?id=603833089963720&helpref=search&sr=1&query=slideshow%20ads) are made up of 3 to 10 images or a single video that plays in a slideshow. These ads are the little cousin to video ads because they use [five times less data](https://www.facebook.com/business/ads/slideshow-ad-format) and are intended to be used in markets where internet connections are generally limited.

Slideshow ads can also be a great stepping stone for people who have no video-making experience but still want to catch the reader’s eye with the movement and sound that makes video ads so effective.

[Best practices](https://www.facebook.com/business/help/347114248961706?id=603833089963720) for slideshow ads:

*   Use high-quality images and videos to make an impact.
*   Insert music (that you have the rights to use).
*   Target slow-internet areas with slideshow versions of your best video ads.

Slideshows share the same specs as [video ads](https://www.facebook.com/business/help/1596868350601716?id=603833089963720).

[](https://adespresso.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/05/Facebook-advertising-03.png)

[_Source_](https://www.facebook.com/business/ads/slideshow-ad-format)

### **Stories ads**

[Stories ads](https://www.facebook.com/business/help/329494947852688?id=2331035843782460) are full-screen immersive experiences that pop up in-between the Stories users watch on Facebook, Instagram, Messenger or WhatsApp. You can make your Stories with videos, images or even carousels.

Stories offer a lot more freedom of expression than your typical video or image ads, as you can experiment with video effects, emojis and even [augmented reality](https://sparkar.facebook.com/ar-studio) to make an impression on your viewers.

The Stories format is great for showing off your brand, but Stories are not placed on Facebook feeds, so they aren’t a silver bullet for advertisers. The media in Stories require different formatting than image or video ads, so you might be forced to make unique content just for Stories, making them more work overall.

[Best practices](https://www.facebook.com/business/help/304846896685564?id=2331035843782460) for Stories ads:

*   Keep the pace of your Stories quick, with frequent switches between different images and videos.
*   Use tools like motion and augmented reality to enhance the viewing experience.
*   Optimize your images and videos to be used on a full screen.

Learn more about [Stories ad specs](https://www.facebook.com/business/help/188477725155524?id=2331035843782460).

# 6 Facebook Ads for Local Businesses That Drive Real Leads

[March 9, 2026](https://actglobalmarketing.com/facebook-ads-for-local-businesses/) [ahsanalsig@gmail.com](https://actglobalmarketing.com/facebook-ads-for-local-businesses/) [Comments(0)](https://actglobalmarketing.com/facebook-ads-for-local-businesses/)

Whether you run a restaurant, HVAC company, real estate agency, or fitness studio, relying only on word-of-mouth is no longer sustainable.

Facebook ads give local businesses something traditional advertising cannot:

• **Precise geo-targeting**  
• **Homeowner and demographic targeting**  
• **AI-driven optimization**  
• **Visual storytelling**

In campaigns we manage for Florida businesses, typical results include:

• **$8 – $25 cost per lead**  
• **3x – 10x return on ad spend**  
• **20 – 100 leads per month**

Facebook is particularly effective because most users check the platform **multiple times per day**, which dramatically increases ad exposure.

* * *

**Pro Tip:**

Local businesses typically generate the best results from Facebook advertising when investing $800–$2,500 per month combined with strong creative and hyper-local targeting.

* * *

## 6 Facebook Ads That Work Best for Local Businesses

### 1\. Local Awareness Ads

**Appeal:** Brand visibility

These ads introduce your business to nearby audiences.

Example:

“Serving Orlando homeowners for 15+ years.”

Local awareness ads help businesses build **trust and familiarity**.

* * *

### 2\. Offer-Driven Ads

**Appeal:** Immediate action

Example:

“20% Off Your First Service”

Discount-driven campaigns often generate **fast conversions**.

Industries that benefit most:

• Restaurants  
• Gyms  
• Beauty salons  
• Auto services

* * *

### 3\. Testimonial Ads

**Appeal:** Social proof

Consumers trust **customer experiences more than brand messaging**.

Example:

“Rated 4.8★ by 300+ Orlando customers.”

These ads are extremely powerful in service industries.

* * *

### 4\. Lead Generation Ads

**Appeal:** Convenience

Lead ads allow users to request quotes **without leaving Facebook**.

This dramatically improves conversion rates.

Common uses:

• Home services  
• Real estate  
• Education programs

* * *

### 5\. Video Story Ads

**Appeal:** Emotional storytelling

Short videos showing behind-the-scenes moments help humanize your brand.

Example:

“Watch how our team restored this 1960s Orlando home.”

* * *

### 6\. Retargeting Ads

**Appeal:** Conversion optimization

Retargeting ads reach users who have:

• visited your website  
• engaged with your page  
• watched your videos

These audiences convert at **much higher rates**.

* * *

## Comparison

| Ad Format | Best Use | Avg CPL |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Video Reels | Brand & Trust Building | $8–$18 |
| Lead Ads | Fast Bookings | $12–$25 |
| DM Ads | Personal Sales | $10–$28 |

* * *

### ✔ Extensions

*   Precise location targeting
*   Highly visual creative opportunities
*   Scales beyond word-of-mouth marketing

### ✖ Limitations

*   Creative quality impacts performance
*   Requires ongoing optimization
*   Needs consistent testing

* * *

## Real Campaign Case Study

### Orlando Local Service Business

**Budget:** $1,500/month

**Campaign duration:** 90 days

**Results:**

*   138 qualified leads
*   48 converted customers
*   $96,000 revenue generated
*   12.4x ROAS

**Key drivers:**

*   Hyper-local audience targeting
*   Video testimonial ads
*   AI-optimized retargeting campaigns

* * *

## 10 FAQs

**1\. Do Facebook ads work for local businesses?**  
Yes. Facebook’s geo-targeting and demographic filters make it ideal for local marketing.

**2\. What budget should local businesses start with?**  
Most campaigns start between $800 and $2,000 per month.

**3\. Are Facebook ads better than boosted posts?**  
Yes, because they offer advanced targeting and optimization.

**4\. Which ad format converts best?**  
Video ads and lead ads usually perform best.

**5\. How fast can leads start coming in?**  
Typically within the first 1–2 weeks.

**6\. Can small businesses compete with larger companies?**  
Yes, especially with hyper-local targeting.

**7\. Should ads run year-round?**  
Yes, but budgets can increase during peak seasons.

**8\. Do visuals matter in Facebook ads?**  
Absolutely. Visual content dramatically increases engagement.

**9\. Are Facebook ads expensive?**  
Compared to traditional advertising, they are extremely cost-effective.

**10\. Do I need a landing page?**  
A strong landing page improves conversion rates significantly.
